title_en: Last Night I Passed By, Mother
en_note: Machine translation by Claude (my reading), not on Pesna.org and not checked by a native speaker. Treat it as a study aid.
translator_notes: Traditional. The raven/nightingale verse is a metaphor (the small girl can manage by herself); 'му' in the raven lines is my reading as 'for him'.

lines.en: - Last night I passed by, mother, I went,
beside a cold clear, mother, well,
beside a cold clear, mother, well.
There I found a girl, mother, a little one,
she was drinking cold water, mother,
she was washing her white face, mother.
Go, dear mother, and ask for her,

lines.cyr: дали ќе ти ја дадат за мене,
lines.lat: dali ḱe ti ja dadat za mene,
lines.en: whether they will give her to you for me,

lines.cyr: дали ќе ти ја дадат за мене?
lines.lat: dali ḱe ti ja dadat za mene?
lines.en: whether they will give her to you for me?
- She is small, my son, hey, Stojan,

lines.cyr: не знае куќа, синко, да гледа,
lines.lat: ne znae kuḱa, sinko, da gleda,
lines.en: she does not know, son, how to keep house,

lines.cyr: не знае куќа, синко, да гледа.
lines.lat: ne znae kuḱa, sinko, da gleda.
lines.en: she does not know, son, how to keep house.
others made a nest for him, mother,
The nightingale is a small bird, mother,
it made its own nest, mother,
it made its own nest, mother.
